claims.text: The initial AlCoCrFeNi eutectic alloy has a coarse, continuous dual-phase FCC/B2 lamellar structure.
The initial lamellar alloy exhibits catastrophic interfacial cracking and low ductility during room-temperature uniaxial tension.
Cold rolling by more than 80% followed by one hour of non-isothermal annealing at 700–740 °C and water quenching can produce the proposed hierarchical architecture.
A heating rate of 10 °C min⁻¹ is suitable for the proposed annealing treatment.
Severe cold rolling introduces high dislocation density and strain gradients into this alloy.
The relevant tensile-testing condition is room temperature at an initial strain rate of 2.5 × 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹.
The treatment produces submicron FCC/B2 grains within FCC lamellae together with micron-scale alternating FCC/B2 lamellae.
The treatment causes phase decomposition into small intragranular P1 precipitates and larger intergranular P2 precipitates.
Interfaces between submicron grains and lamellae store geometrically necessary dislocations because of strain gradients.
Stored geometrically necessary dislocations generate long-range back-stress and sustained strain hardening.
Aligned lamellae and ductile precipitates arrest microcracks, inhibit crack coalescence, and relieve interfacial stress concentrations.
The treated alloy can attain a yield strength of approximately 1.5 GPa and an elongation of approximately 16%.
The treatment simultaneously improves strength and ductility relative to as-cast and ultrafine-grained counterparts.
The treatment significantly reduces interfacial cracking and changes failure from brittle to ductile.
The continuous-lamellar baseline has high strength but low ductility because of catastrophic interfacial cracking and lacks a hierarchical constraint effect.
Annealing above 900 °C degrades the lamellar structure and causes inferior tensile properties.
Precipitates must remain in the nanoscale-to-micron-scale range because coarse band-like precipitates initiate rather than arrest microcracks.
HIP at 1100 °C and 100 MPa for two hours will homogenize the alloy without producing the hierarchical strain gradients induced by severe rolling.
A comparison between the proposed rolling/annealing route and the specified HIP route isolates extreme pressure as the causal variable.
Equivalent or superior HIP performance would falsify the claim that the specific thermomechanical path is required for the strength–ductility synergy.

contradictions.description: The central hypothesis attributes the benefit to the severe-deformation/annealing path and its hierarchical strain gradients, but part of the falsification rule refers instead to falsifying a hypothesis that extreme pressure or HIP is the primary driver.

The rule first says that equivalent or superior HIP performance would falsify extreme pressure as the primary driver, but later says that better HIP performance would falsify the requirement for the specific thermomechanical path. Equivalent or superior HIP performance would not logically falsify a pressure-driven explanation.

The experiment is described as isolating extreme pressure, but the two sets also differ in deformation history, temperature, duration, and intended microstructure, so pressure is not the only changed variable.
